$comment: LICENSE-PENDING — see docs/non_ratified/LICENSE_PENDING.md. Grant per FB-RAT-AUTH-001/002/004/005/006/007 (GRANT MODEL: principal + actions + resource scope + constraints + expiry + confirmation policy + delegation rule). Typically carried as the `payload` of a ContractEnvelope<Grant> (see schemas/common/envelope.schema.json) — `grantId` below is this object's own FB-RAT-COM-002 stable ID, distinct from the envelope's objectId. `grantId` is also the exact string schemas/execution/request.schema.json's `authorityGrant.grantId` field references (FB-RAT-COM-012 'no contract bypass') — see docs/ratified/CAPABILITY_AUTHORITY_MODEL.md §11 for that cross-domain correlation.
title: Grant
description: A scoped authorization: WHO (principalId) may do WHAT (capabilityIds, all resolving to the same authorityRung) to WHICH resource (resourceScope), under WHAT constraints, until WHEN (expiresAtUtc), with WHAT confirmation policy, and WHETHER a child principal may inherit it (delegationRule). capabilityIds MUST be drawn from schemas/loops/registries/capability-ids.v1.json's reverse-DNS fb.* namespace — that registry is the concrete capability-ID vocabulary this general authority model is written against; it is not redefined here.

grantId.description: Globally unique stable ID for this grant (FB-RAT-COM-002).

principalId.description: References a Principal.principalId (schemas/authority/principal.schema.json) — the principal this grant authorizes. This schema does not itself join against a Principal store to verify the reference resolves; that is a decision-engine-time obligation, same pattern as ArtifactRef.producerReceipt in schemas/common/artifact-ref.schema.json.

capabilityIds.description: One or more reverse-DNS capability IDs from schemas/loops/registries/capability-ids.v1.json (e.g. 'fb.repo.commit', 'fb.model.cloud_inference'). This schema cannot itself join against that external registry to confirm every ID is a real, registered capability, or that every one resolves to the SAME `authorityRung` declared below — that cross-registry check is a decision-engine-time obligation (see fixtures/authority/adversarial/grant-authorityrung-capability-mismatch.adversarial.json). A policy that needs to grant capabilities spanning more than one rung MUST issue one Grant per rung, never a single Grant mixing rungs — this keeps 'is this grant at or below the rung this delegation would need' a single field comparison (see `delegationRule` below) instead of a per-capability lookup.

authorityRung.description: FB-RAT-AUTH-002: the single authority-ladder rung every entry in `capabilityIds` resolves to per capability-ids.v1.json. Also the ceiling `delegationRule.maxDelegatedRung` is checked against, structurally, below.

resourceScope.description: FB-RAT-AUTH-005 target-binding: exactly which resource instance(s) this grant applies to. A grant with a broad `locator` (e.g. a wide file glob, or a wildcard network domain) is a legitimate but wider grant — narrowing is always a decision the ISSUER made explicit here, never an ambient default.

purpose.description: FB-RAT-AUTH-005 purpose-binding tag, e.g. 'model-provider-authentication', 'git-push-to-user-selected-remote'. MUST be non-null for any capability whose capability-ids.v1.json entry has `requiresPurposeBinding: true` (this schema cannot enforce that cross-registry rule structurally — see fixtures/authority/adversarial/decision-purpose-crossing-secret-use.adversarial.json, which models a policy engine catching exactly this at decision time). A secret-use grant purpose-bound to 'model-provider-authentication' MUST NOT be usable to authorize an unrelated shell/network operation, even against the same underlying resourceScope — purpose is a second, independent binding axis on top of resourceScope, not a synonym for it.

additionalConstraints.description: Open bag for constraint dimensions this general model does not enumerate by name (e.g. a max-invocation-count, a rate limit, a byte-size ceiling on a secret's use). Kept open rather than closed because concrete constraint vocabularies are expected to be domain-specific (execution/device/loop budget dimensions already have their own richer shapes — this is not meant to duplicate schemas/execution/request.schema.json's `budget`).

expiresAtUtc.description: FB-RAT-AUTH-005: every grant is time-bound — there is no shape of this contract representing a non-expiring grant. A grant intended to last 'until revoked' still MUST carry a concrete, reissuable expiry (renewal is a fresh Grant with a fresh `grantId` and fresh `expiresAtUtc`, an explicit act, never a silent extension of this one — see fixtures/authority/adversarial/decision-request-against-expired-grant.adversarial.json, FB-RAT-AUTH-003/005: a request against an expired grant MUST decide DENY, not silently renew).

unknownFields.description: Bag for fields a decoder received but did not recognize, preserved for round-trip (FB-RAT-COM-003).

AuthorityRung.description: FB-RAT-AUTH-002's eight-rung authority ladder, in ascending order. Identical to capability-ids.v1.json's top-level `authorityLadder` array — duplicated here per this repo's established convention of duplicating small closed-vocabulary $defs across schema files rather than reaching into another document's $defs for an in-repo (non-`schemas/common/`) reference (see docs/ratified/COMMON_CONVENTIONS.md §5, and schemas/execution/request.schema.json's duplicated `FgsType` for a precedent). Both copies MUST be kept in sync if this ladder changes — a ladder change is a FB-RAT-AUTH-002 decision amendment, not a routine edit.

kind.description: Closed vocabulary from the GRANT MODEL resources list. WORKSPACE_ROOT: a whole Workspace (schemas/workspace/workspace.schema.json). FILE_GLOB: a path pattern within a workspace/repository. REPOSITORY: a specific git-hosted repo. EXECUTION_TARGET: a specific schemas/execution/target.schema.json id. NETWORK_DOMAIN: a specific host (e.g. an API provider, or the ASOM local daemon at 127.0.0.1:11435 — see docs/ratified/CAPABILITY_AUTHORITY_MODEL.md §11.2). SECRET: a specific Keystore-held secret handle (never the raw value — see security/KeystoreSecret.kt). DEVICE: a specific connected USB/serial device. RELEASE: a specific app/store release artifact. STORE_CHANNEL: a specific distribution channel (e.g. Play internal-testing track).

locator.description: Kind-specific identifier or pattern: a Workspace.id (WORKSPACE_ROOT), a glob string (FILE_GLOB), a repository id/URL (REPOSITORY), an ExecutionTarget.id (EXECUTION_TARGET), a hostname (NETWORK_DOMAIN), a secret handle id — never a raw secret value (SECRET; see fixtures/authority/adversarial for the sibling secret-leak pattern already established at fixtures/common/adversarial/error-secret-leak-in-detail and fixtures/execution/adversarial/receipt-secret-leak-in-log-excerpt), a device id (DEVICE), a release id (RELEASE), a channel id (STORE_CHANNEL).

mode.description: Whether exercising this grant ever produces a REQUIRE_CONFIRMATION decision outcome (schemas/authority/decision.schema.json): NEVER_REQUIRED (e.g. a narrow, low-risk OBSERVE/READ grant), ALWAYS_REQUIRED (every use pauses for a fresh user confirmation — appropriate for FB-RAT-AUTH-006 visible-high-risk-authority operations), REQUIRED_ABOVE_RUNG (confirmation is required only when a specific use of this grant would need `aboveRung` or higher — relevant when a grant's `capabilityIds` legitimately span behaviors a decision engine treats at finer granularity than the single `authorityRung` ceiling declared above).

aboveRung.description: Required non-null only when `mode` is REQUIRED_ABOVE_RUNG (see the if/then below); null for NEVER_REQUIRED/ALWAYS_REQUIRED, where it is meaningless.

delegable.description: Whether a child principal of this grant's `principalId` (per Principal.parentPrincipalId, schemas/authority/principal.schema.json) may be issued its OWN grant deriving from this one. This field does not itself perform delegation — it only records whether the issuing policy permits it; the actual child grant is still a separate, freshly-issued Grant object (see `transitiveDelegationAllowed` below for why).

maxDelegatedRung.description: Required non-null when `delegable` is true, required null when `delegable` is false (see the if/then below). When non-null, this schema's top-level `allOf` structurally forbids it from exceeding this Grant's own `authorityRung` — FB-RAT-AUTH-004 ('no implicit privilege expansion') encoded as a field-level ceiling a schema-valid document cannot violate, not left as prose alone.

transitiveDelegationAllowed.description: FB-RAT-AUTH-007 — REJECTED: automatic/transitive delegation (a grant flowing from principal A to child B to B's own child C without a fresh, independently-issued grant at each hop) is structurally disallowed. This field is pinned to `false` on every Grant in this contract version; there is no schema-valid way to declare a Grant that re-delegates itself down a chain. A grandchild principal that needs authority gets its OWN Grant, issued fresh (typically requiring a fresh user escalation per `requiresFreshUserApprovalForWidening`), never an inherited copy of an ancestor's Grant. See fixtures/authority/invalid/grant-transitive-delegation-flag-rejected.invalid.json (this field set `true` is a structural — not merely semantic — validation failure) and fixtures/authority/adversarial/decision-transitive-delegation-attempt.adversarial.json (the decision-time consequence when a request tries to exploit this anyway).

requiresFreshUserApprovalForWidening.description: FB-RAT-AUTH-004/007: any attempt to grant a child principal MORE authority than this Grant itself carries (a 'widening' delegation) requires an explicit, fresh user approval action — never an automatic consequence of this Grant existing. Pinned to `true` on every Grant in this contract version for the same reason `transitiveDelegationAllowed` is pinned to `false`: this invariant is meant to be unconditional, so it is encoded as a constant rather than a togglable policy field.
